National Highway Authority of India, (Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Govt. of India),
through its Project Director, Project Implementation Unit, Kanhari Hill Road, Hazaribagh (Jharkhand)- 825301 .... .... .... Opposite Party/Appellant Versus 1. Dwarika Sao, s/o late Rameshwar Sao, R/o village Singhrawan P.S. Chauparan, District Hazaribagh.
2. Shanti Devi, wife of Late Baban Sao, R/o village Singhrawan, P.S. Chauparan, District Hazaribagh.
.... .... .... Petitioners/Respondents 3. The State of Jharkhand, through Deputy Commissioner, Hazaribagh, P.O., P.S. & District Hazaribagh.
.... .... .... Opposite Party No.1/Performa Respondent ------
 For the Appellant : Mrs. Sweety Topno, Advocate  Mr. Amrit Raj Kisku, Advocate  For the Respondents : Mr. Sachin Kumar, AC to SC-I  Mr. Yogendra Prasad, Advocate  Mr. Sanjay Kr. Tiwari, Advocate  ------

sentences.text: By the Court:- Heard the parties.

2. This First Appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, has been preferred by the appellant being aggrieved by the judgment dated 23.07.2016 passed by the Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh in L.R. Case No.11 of 2007 and the award prepared on the basis of the said judgment, which was signed on 05.08.2016, on the basis of the estimate made by the Junior Engineer, Building Division, and further held that both the respondent Nos.1 and 2 are entitled to 30% solatium thereon and 12% interest from the date of notification to the date of award or to take possession; whichever is earlier.

Over and above, the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition,
Hazaribagh has also held that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 are entitled to get 9% of access of land of compensation for the first time after taking possession and will get interest thereon 15% per annum till realization of the compensation, and allowed the land reference case in part.

3. The brief fact of the case is that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 who are the petitioners before the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh, are the owners of the building/structure which was situated over the land which was acquired by the appellant for widening of National Highway, for which notice under Section 12 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was served upon the respondent No.1 and husband of the respondent No.2 namely Baban Sao (since deceased).
Baban Sao received a compensation amount of Rs.5,531/- for the land value along with interest at the rate of 12% and solatium of 30%.

4. The case of the respondents is that the respondent No.1 and the husband of the respondent No.2 built buildings for residential-cum-commercial purpose over the said land and were carrying on business of general store cum parchune.

It is further the case of the respondent Nos.1 and 2 of this appeal that the building which has been acquisitioned, has been marked 20'width north to south and 32'east to west but the actual building which was affected by acquisition is 27.6" X 32'.

Further,
the case of the petitioner is that the compensation of the land has been awarded but the compensation of the building has not been prepared, due to mistake of the concerned Assessing Authority, for which the petitioner sustained damage of the said acquisitioned land and building and, therefore, the petitioner claimed compensation in respect of the building which has been acquisitioned.

5. In their written statement, the opposite party No.1 before the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh who is the proforma respondent No.3 herein challenged the maintainability of the claim of the petitioner on various technical grounds and a general denial of the claims made by the petitioner before the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh; was made by the opposite party No.1, before the Special Judge.

The appellant who was the opposite party No.2 before the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh, in its written statement, admitted acquisition of the land and also pleaded as the District Land Acquisition Officer, Hazaribagh placed the demand of compensation of the land in village for disbursement of compensation.
The appellant herein deposited the amount towards compensation of acquisition of land.

Consequent upon that,
the District Land Acquisition Officer, Hazaribagh handed over the certificate of compensation of the land.

The appellant/opposite party No.2 admitted the acquisition of 7 decimals of land of the respondent No.1 and the husband of the respondent No.2 for which compensation of Rs.5,531/- in National Highway Authority Of India vs Dwarika Sao on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197967572/
2

sentences.text: L.A. Case No.2/03-04
under award No.131 to Dwarika Sao and Baban Sao was made.
The appellant/opposite party No.2 has no role in connection of the award.

It was also pleaded by the appellant/opposite party No.2 that compensation of building or dwelling house on the part of the plot No.1000/2, Khata No.45, Mouja Singhrawan for Rs.2,36,125/- under the award No.131 to the respondent/petitioner No.1 namely Dwarika Saw and Rs.89,603/- under the award No.132 to Baban Sao- husband of respondent/petitioner No.2 was separately made.
The opposite party No.2 has no role regarding determination of compensation.
6. In support of their case, the petitioners examined 6 witnesses and proved the documents which have been marked as Ext.I to VI.
From the side of the opposite parties, 1 witness was examined and 3 documents were marked as Ext.A, B and C.

On the basis of the pleadings of the rival parties, the two points for consideration were framed by the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribag which are as under: -
(i) Whether this land reference case mentioned as above is maintainable in its present form or not?
(ii) Whether the petitioners in the said reference case are entitled to get any compensation in respect of their claim or not?

If so, to what extent?
7.
The learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh considered the evidence in the record and observed that on Khata No.1000/2, there were two buildings constructed.

The Amin measured the same and valuation of the building was done by the Executive Engineer, Building Division and the report of the Executive Engineer was in the record before the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh.

From the report of the Junior Engineer, Building Division marked Ext.6,
the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh found that the building of petitioner/respondent No.2 namely Shanti Devi situated over plot No.1000/2, Khata No.45 has been valued as Rs.2,98,884/- and the valuation of the building of the petitioner/respondent No.1 as per the report of the Junior Engineer was mentioned as Rs.4,97,484/-.
8.

The learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh also considered the sale-deed of the year 2002 which has been marked as Ext.3 which shows that 6 decimals of land were sold for consideration of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Similarly, Ext.3/A another sale-deed revealed that 8 decimals of land were sold for a total consideration amount of Rs.1,60,000/-.

The learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh considered the reference as has been made for enhancement of awarded amount and also for compensation of two buildings which were situated on the said land.

The learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh also considered the testimony of PW-1 namely Manoj Kumar, in paragraph-5 of his deposition, to the effect that the award was prepared in respect of the land but the award for the building was not prepared.

9. It is pertinent to mention here that though not specifically mentioned in the impugned judgment,
the perusal of the deposition of PW-1 reveals that there is absolutely no cross-examination of P.W.1 in respect of his examination in chief that the award for the building was not prepared.

Thus both portions of the testimony of PW-1 that the award was made only for the land and not for the National Highway Authority Of India vs Dwarika Sao on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197967572/
3 building remains unchallenged, hence is to be accepted.

sentences.text: 10. The learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh also considered the testimony of PW-2 namely Shankar Sao in paragraph-5 of his deposition where he has also stated that the award was prepared for the land only but the award for the building was not prepared.

Perusal of the record reveals that there is absolutely no cross-examination of the PW-2 in respect of the said statement made by the PW-2 in paragraph-5 of this deposition inter alia to the effect that the award for the building was not prepared.

11. The learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh also considered the testimony of PW-3- the petitioner/respondent No.1 namely Dwarika Sao that the affected area of the building is 27'6"X 32' and no award was prepared in respect of the building nor any compensation was paid to him in respect of the building.

The perusal of the cross-examination of PW-3 reveals that though he was cross-examined by the appellant/opposite party No.2 but neither his testimony that the petitioners have not been paid compensation in respect of the building which exists over the acquired land nor his testimony that the building of the petitioners in excess of the earmarked area of 20" X 23" i.e.
20"
X 32" but in fact, 27'6" has been affected; was specifically challenged in his cross-examination.

There is no suggestion even given by the appellant/opposite party No.2 in the cross-examination to the PW-3 of the case of the appellant that R s . 2 , 3 6 , 1 2 5 / - w a s g i v e n a s c o m p e n s a t i o n t o t h e P W - 3 w h o i s t h e petitioner/respondent No.1.
12.

The learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh also considered the deposition of PW-4 namely Shanti Devi to the same effect that only compensation for the land was given and not for the building and the affected building/structure is more than the earmarked one.

Though it is the specific case of the appellant-opposite party No.2 in the written-statement that a sum of Rs.89,603/- was paid to the husband of Shanti Devi in respect of the building but in the cross-examination, no such suggestion was given to the PW-4.
13.

After considering the evidence in the record which has been discussed in the impugned judgment, the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh found and held that the petitioners before it are not entitled for enhancement of the compensation amount in respect of the acquired land but they are entitled for enhancement for affected portion of the building and relying upon the Ext.6 i.e. the calculation made by the Junior Engineer, Building Division; which was also remained unchallenged, during the proceeding before it, the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh, partly allowed the claim for the compensation in respect of the building/structure of the acquired land and answered the point for determination No.2 accordingly.
14.

The learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh next took up the point for consideration No.1 and considering the fact that no compensation was paid for the two buildings which were left out which is existing over the acquired land and the valuation of the building was done by the Junior Engineer, Building Division, Hazaribagh and as the case was filed within the National Highway Authority Of India vs Dwarika Sao on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197967572/
4 stipulated period, as enumerated in the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, held that the reference case was maintainable in its present form and passed the order regarding entitlement as already indicated above.
15.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the judgment and award passed by the learned court below is erroneous, and also submits that the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition,
Hazaribagh

failed to consider the fact of payment of compensation for the building which has been received by the petitioner/respondent No.1 herein, and the husband of the respondent/petitioner No.2 vide award No.131 and 132 respectively, for the constructed house
. It is next submitted that the learned court below erroneously awarded solatium and interest.
It is also submitted that the learned court below failed to consider that the evidence of the petitioners was full of contradictions vis--vis the documents exhibited by them.

16. It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh failed to consider the Ext.B which is the proper assessment of compensation, need not require any interference.

Hence, it is submitted that this appeal be allowed and the judgment dated 23.07.2016 and award dated 05.08.2016 passed by the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh in L.R. Case No.11/2007, be set aside.

17. Learned counsel for the respondents on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer of the appellant to set aside the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh and submits that so far as the contention of the appellant regarding Ext.B is concerned, the Ext.B is the proceedings of the Land Acquisition Case No.02 of 2003-04 wherein the compensation of the land only has been calculated and the said payment of compensation for the land to the petitioner No.1 who is the respondent No.2 here in for Rs.5,531/- which the petitioner No.1 has admitted categorically, so there is no way, the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition,
Hazaribagh has committed any error, so far as the contention of the appellant regarding Ext.6 is concerned.

18. Learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1 and 2 submits that the Ext.6 is the report of the Junior Engineer wherein he has assessed the valuation of the affected property of the petitioner/respondents but nowhere shows any payment of compensation for the building to either of the petitioner/respondents No.1 and 2.
19.

Learned counsel for the respondents next submits that there is absolutely no material available in the record to show that any compensation has been paid to the petitioner/respondents in respect of the buildings/structure existing over the acquired land and the undisputed facts remains that the buildings/structure was existing over the acquired land which is evident from the unchallenged report of the Junior Engineer, Building Division, Hazaribagh which has been marked as Ext.6.
20.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1 and 2 that there is absolutely no cross-examination of any of the witnesses of the petitioners wherein they have categorically stated that no compensation has been paid to them in respect of the building and such portion of the testimony has even not been challenged in the respective cross-examination of the National Highway Authority Of India vs Dwarika Sao on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197967572/
5 witnesses, by the appellant or the proforma respondent No.3 who were respectively opposite party Nos.2 and 1 before the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh.

sentences.text:
Hence, it is submitted that no illegality having been committed by the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition,
Hazaribagh; this appeal, being without any merit, be dismissed.
21. Having heard the rival submissions made at the Bar and after carefully going through the materials available in the record, the following points for determination that crop up in this appeal is:-

"Whether the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh has committed any illegality by not accepting the contention of the appellant in respect of the acquisition of the building/structure existing over the land in question?
Whether the petitioner/respondent No.1 has been paid Rs.2,36,125/- and the husband of the petitioner/respondent No.2 was paid Rs.89,603/- respectively?"

22. After going through the materials available in the record, it is crystal clear that it is a specific case of the appellant/opposite party No.2 that such amount was paid to the petitioner/respondents but it is pertinent to mention here that as already indicated above in the foregoing paragraph of the judgment though the witnesses of the petitioner/respondent Nos.1 and 2 have categorically stated that they have not been paid any compensation in respect of the building but they were cross-examined by the appellant/opposite party No.2 also besides the opposite party No.1 who is the proforma respondent No.3 of this appeal, but such testimony of the witnesses of the petitioners including petitioner/respondent No.1 themselves, who has been examined as PW-3 and PW-4 respectively, have not been challenged in their respective cross-examination and consequence is that the same is to be accepted to be true.
23.

Further, without any plausible reason, no one entered into witness box on behalf of the opposite party No.2 to support the contention of the opposite party No.2 to establish the contention of the opposite party No.2 regarding payment of compensation to the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 in respect of the land/structure existing over the acquired land, nor any document was brought in evidence in support of such contention.

24. Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that in view of the unchallenged testimony of the petitioners, the unchallenged report of the Junior Engineer, Building Division,
Hazaribagh which has been marked as Ext.6 and in the absence of any evidence put forth by the appellant/opposite party No.2 in support of its contention of payment of any compensation to the petitioners in respect of the building
, this Court do not find any illegality having been committed by the learned Special Judge, Land Acquisition, Hazaribagh in passing the impugned judgment and award.
25. Accordingly, this appeal, being without any merit, is dismissed on contest.
